intro: Texas runs its elections county by county, through a county elections administrator or the county clerk and tax assessor-collector.

elections.name: General election
elections.what: Federal, state, county, and judicial offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Last day to register to vote
dates.detail: A mailed application had to be postmarked by this date. Texas has no same-day registration.

dates.label: Early voting
dates.detail: Vote at any early-voting site in your county of registration.

dates.label: Mail ballot application must be received
dates.detail: The early voting clerk must have it by close of business or noon, whichever is later. Voting by mail in Texas is limited — for example, to voters who are 65 or older, disabled, or out of the county during the election.

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 7 am to 7 pm. A mail ballot must be postmarked by 7 pm and arrive by 5 pm on Wednesday, Nov. 4.

id_rule.text: Bring one of the approved photo IDs — a Texas driver's license or ID card, a Texas handgun license, a U.S. passport, military ID, citizenship certificate, or Texas election ID certificate. If you can't reasonably get one, you can sign a reasonable impediment declaration and show another document, such as a utility bill or bank statement.
